cover.title: Design a scalable Food Delivery App
cover.subtitle: Zomato / Swiggy system design
cover.tagline: One case study, three actors: customer, restaurant, delivery partner

rows: discover, view menu, order, pay, track, cancel, rate

items: 50M MAU, 10M DAU, ==3M orders/day==; peak is about 4x average
Orders: ~35/s average, ~150/s dinner peak
Reads: 20 browses/order = 60M/day, ~700 QPS avg, ~3,000 QPS peak
Tracking: 300K partners every 5 s = ~60K writes/s

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Every order needs all 3 sides to say yes at once. State scope, then numbers: ~150 orders/s but ~60K location writes/s, so tracking is the write-heavy part. Be strict only where money moves.

items: ==Clients==: customer app, restaurant tablet, partner app
All traffic enters via **CDN** and an ==API gateway== (auth, rate limit, routing)
==Core services==: user, restaurant/menu, search, cart, order
Plus payment, dispatch, tracking and notification services
Checkout path uses ==sync== REST/gRPC: the user waits for a result
Everything downstream goes ==async== as events on **Kafka**
`OrderPlaced` fans out to payment, restaurant, dispatch, notification
Analytics also consumes it, so no extra call from order

blocks.title: Database per service
items: Avoids ==shared-schema== coupling between teams
Each service deploys and scales its own store
Trade-off: **no cross-service joins**
So use events and ==sagas== to stay consistent

blocks.title: Cross-cutting concerns
items: ==Service discovery== so services find each other
**Circuit breakers** stop cascading failures
Tracing with one ==correlation ID== per request
Config and ==feature flags== change behaviour safely
==Order== service: the source of truth, own DB
==Payment== service: strict isolation for money
==Dispatch==: spiky load, scales on its own

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Start as a modular monolith, then split order, payment and dispatch first: sync for checkout, Kafka events for the rest.

items: Find restaurants and dishes by ==location==, cuisine, name, rating, price, ETA, open status
{icon:map-pin} Geohash or H3 cells (~1-5 km) map user location to nearby restaurants
{icon:elasticsearch} ES index: `geo_point` plus text fields for restaurant, dish, cuisine
Rank by blending **relevance**, rating, ETA and promotion
__Serviceability__: keep restaurants whose radius and live partner supply cover the user

redis.text: Redis: open, ETA, hot cells 60 s TTL

items: **ES down**: fall back to cached results per geohash cell
Stale menu shows sold-out item: re-validate at ==cart==
Search p99 under **300 ms**; zero-result rate stays low
Track click-through rate and index lag in seconds
Cache hit ratio over **80%** on hot cells
Menu and open-status edits reach ES via ==CDC== in ~5 s
Hot geohash cells cached in Redis, **60 s** TTL
Cursor pagination keeps result pages stable

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Geo cells narrow candidates, ES ranks them, Redis keeps open status live.

items: Owns the ==order lifecycle== from cart checkout to delivery
Is the **source of truth** for every order's status
Orchestrates payment, restaurant and dispatch, never does their work
Sibling tables: `order_items` and `order_events`, sharded by `user_id`
Each transition appends an `order_events` row
Gives an ==audit trail== and replayable history

blocks.title: 5. Key APIs
items: `POST /v1/orders` creates an order
`GET /v1/orders/{id}` reads current status
`POST /v1/orders/{id}/cancel` by customer
`PATCH /v1/orders/{id}/status` for restaurant and partner

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency
items: Client sends an `Idempotency-Key` with `POST /v1/orders`
Server keeps a unique key to order id map
A retry returns the **same** order, no duplicate

blocks.title: 7. Failures and Metrics
items: Restaurant must accept in ==3 min==, else auto-cancel and refund
Duplicate events: idempotent consumers make repeats no-ops
__Sweeper job__ scans non-terminal orders older than 30 min
Metrics: success >99%, accept rate, cancels by reason, stuck count
Only legal transitions pass the compare-and-set update
Cancel is free until the restaurant accepts
Track time in each state to spot slow stages
Idempotent writes make client retries safe

blocks.title: Interview tip:
blocks.text: Say the CAS line out loud: WHERE id=? AND status=? makes races safe.

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: One DB row plus compare-and-set status updates gives safe, auditable order flow.

items: Hold items, price them, apply ==coupons== and fees, output a final quote
Cart is a Redis hash keyed by `user_id`, 24 h TTL
One cart holds items from **one** restaurant only
==Quote== = items + packaging + delivery + taxes − discount
Delivery fee follows distance and **surge**; every amount is integer paise
Checkout re-checks live menu price, availability, open status, serviceability
Quote is locked 10 min under a `quote_id`: shown = charged
Coupon checks: min order value, per-user limit, expiry

rows: one cart per user, TTL 24 h

items: Item sold out before pay: **409** with a changed-items diff
Redis loss is fine: client rebuilds cart from its copy
Coupon usage reserved atomically: Redis Lua script or DB row lock
Track cart-to-order conversion (~25%) and checkout abandonment
Alert on price-mismatch rate and coupon failure rate

blocks.title: Interview tip:
blocks.text: Cart can be lost safely, but the locked quote and coupon reservation must be atomic.

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Re-validate at checkout, then lock the quote for 10 min so the price shown is the price charged.

items: Charge, refund and ==reconcile== via gateways: UPI, cards, wallets, COD
Never store raw card data, only **tokens**
Own the payment state; the order service only reacts to it
Webhook is the ==source of truth==; redirects can be lost
Verify the webhook **signature**, and also poll status
==Idempotency key== per attempt stops a double charge on retry

blocks.title: Saga
blocks.text: SUCCESS triggers PLACED. Restaurant rejects: compensating refund runs. Payment timeout: order cancelled.

items: Gateway timeout leaves state ==unknown==: query gateway before retrying
Nightly job matches gateway settlement files with the **ledger**
Track success rate above 97% and gateway latency p99
Track webhook delay, refund time and reconciliation mismatch count
Restaurant rejects: ==compensating refund== runs automatically
Payment timeout: order is cancelled, no charge kept
Every refund writes an **append-only** ledger entry

blocks.title: Interview tip:
blocks.text: Never trust the client redirect: confirm via signed webhook, then poll as backup.

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Trust the signed webhook, retry with an idempotency key, and reconcile nightly.

items: Pick best free partner, cut ==wait at the restaurant==
Search: Redis GEO `GEOSEARCH` 3 km, online, not busy
Score: pickup distance, rating, load, restaurant prep-time
Dispatch fires at ==60-70% of prep time==, not at placement
Offer goes to top-scored partner first
==Batching==: one partner carries 2 nearby orders, detour under 5 minutes

blocks.note: NX gives one winner per order

items: No partner free: raise incentive, then retry
Offline mid-order: ==reassign==; app crash: missed heartbeat
Track assignment time **p50** under 30 s, acceptance rate
Also idle time, orders per partner per hour, batching rate

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Dispatch late, score on prep time, and lock with SET NX so each order gets one partner.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Ingest ==partner GPS== pings from every active rider
Show **live position** on the customer's map
Keep the ==ETA== fresh as the rider moves

blocks.title: 3. Ingest and smoothing
items: Partner app pings every ==5 s==: ~**60K writes/s** at peak
Location gateway batches pings into Kafka
==Map-matching== snaps noisy GPS onto the road network
Send only if the move exceeds **20 m**: saves battery

blocks.title: 4. Push and ETA
items: Push over ==WebSocket or SSE== on topic `order:{id}`
No socket? Client **polls every 10 s**
ETA = rider→restaurant + prep left + restaurant→customer
Routing engine adds live traffic to each route leg

blocks.title: 7. Failure scenarios
items: Rider in a tunnel: show last known position, ==stale badge==
WebSocket node dies: client **reconnects with backoff**, resumes last state

blocks.title: 8. Key metrics
items: Location-to-screen latency under ==2 s==
ETA error (MAE) under **3 min**
Socket connections per node
Dropped pings percent
Stale badge once the last ping is over 30 s old
Reconnect resumes from last known state

blocks.title: Interview tip:
blocks.text: Latest position lives in Redis with a 30 s TTL; history goes to cold store.

items: Tell customers, restaurants and partners about ==order events==
Four channels: push, SMS, email and in-app inbox
Consume order and delivery events from {icon:apachekafka} Kafka, map each to a template
Transactional messages (OTP, order confirmed) always go through
==Push== via FCM/APNs first; SMS fallback for OTP and order confirmed
One queue per channel, workers with rate limits and **exponential backoff** retries
Redis key `(order_id, event_type, user_id)` stops a replayed event sending twice
Quiet hours and opt-outs respected, but ==transactional== always sent

rows: id, user_id, channel, template_id, payload, status, sent_at

items: Internal `POST /v1/notify`: user, template, payload, channel hint
`POST /v1/devices` registers or refreshes an FCM/APNs token
Provider delivery callbacks move SENT to ==DELIVERED== or FAILED
FCM outage: fall back to SMS for **critical** events only
Invalid token: provider returns an error, so the token is removed
SMS cost spike: capped by per-day and per-campaign ==budgets==
Retries use backoff with ==jitter==
Dead-letter queue is replayed after the fix
Token removed on an invalid-token error

blocks.title: Interview tip:
blocks.text: Dedupe key plus idempotent consumers means a replayed Kafka event never double-notifies.

blocks.title: METRICS TO WATCH:
blocks.text: Delivery rate, push-to-display under 3 s for transactional, opt-out rate, DLQ depth, cost per notification.

items: Peak reads ~3,000 QPS: ==cache hit rate== above 90% keeps DB calm
Kafka partitioned by `order_id` keeps **per-order** ordering
Different orders run in parallel across partitions
Pre-scale before the ==7-10 pm== dinner and match-day peaks
Queue-based **load levelling** smooths the ~150 orders/s spike
Shed non-critical load first: recommendations, banners
Timeouts, retries with __jitter__, circuit breakers, bulkheads
Search or tracking down? Degrade gracefully: cached list, polling

blocks.title: Blast radius
blocks.text: A **city cell** outage hits one region only. Multi-AZ fails over inside each cell.

Most people freeze at "design Zomato." Here's the whole thing, broken into handwritten notes you can actually follow, page by page.

What's inside:
📝 Problem, scope and requirements
🏗️ High-level architecture
🔍 Restaurant discovery and search
📦 Order service and state machine
🛒 Cart and checkout
💳 Payments
🛵 Delivery partner assignment
📍 Real-time order tracking
🔔 Notifications
⚖️ Scaling, failure handling and interview questions
